To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a brief (10-ms) electric field can suppress epilept-form activity in the rat hippocampus, that this suppression is independent of field polarity and is uncorrelated to population activity, that the suppression persists during blockade of synaptic transmissions, and that the suppression depends on alignment of the field with the somatodendritic axis of the pyramidal cells and can be related to attenuation of the depo-larizing afterpotentials following action potentials.
a single 10 ms duration electric field suppresses epileptiform activity for several seconds in rat hippocampi in vitro.

a single short-duration (10 ms) electric field applied to the hippocampus suppresses epileptiform activity and that the suppression is related to changes in the membrane properties of CA1 pyrampidal cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new therapeutic method to suppress epileptiform brain activity.
the mechanisms of action of electric field stimulation in epilepsy and other diseases.
the mechanisms of electrical stimulation of brain in epilepsy and related disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the suppressive effect of brief electric fields is due to a combination of effects on membrane properties and synaptic transmission, and that it is not mediated by activation of purinergic receptors.
a brief electric DC field suppresses epileptiform activity.
the suppression of epileptic seizures by electrical brain stimulation is a complex phenomenon that involves multiple mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the therapeutic effects of DC stimulation of the brain can be mediated by a brief, unbalanced electric field, which can be delivered through a single electrode.
a brief electric stimulus can induce a long-lasting effect on the neuronal membrane properties, which may explain the therapeutic effects of brain stimulation.
a short-duration, balanced electric field, when applied to the brain during epileptic activity, can suppress hyperexcitability and reduce the duration of epileptic events.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the therapeutic effects of brain stimulation in epilepsy and other brain disorders are unlikely to be due to direct polarizing effects on neuronal membranes.
the therapeutic effect of electrical stimulation of brain in epilepsy can be explained by a direct polarizing action on neuronal membranes.
a brief electric stimulus can suppress the epileptiform discharges.
